eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus heavily favors a 22°C high in Mexico City today, reflecting model consensus from official sources projecting a peak near that threshold amid persistent cloud cover and showers.** 

Mexico City’s high-elevation subtropical highland climate typically produces August daily highs around 23°C, with the warmest point of the day occurring in the mid-afternoon. Current conditions—overcast skies, 70–80% rain probability, and light northerly winds—have suppressed temperatures slightly below seasonal norms, keeping the expected maximum in the narrow 19–23°C band according to multiple forecast runs. The strong market-implied probability for exactly 22°C captures this tight clustering around the most probable observed value once official station data are recorded. 

Realistic scenarios that could shift the outcome include stronger-than-expected afternoon clearing, which might allow brief warming toward 24°C, or heavier persistent rain that caps the high closer to 20°C; both remain low-probability given the stable steering pattern and model agreement.

For 24 August, model guidance and local forecasts converge on partly cloudy skies with southeasterly winds of 10–15 km/h, limiting afternoon heating while high humidity (dew points near 24–26 °C) and any late-day thundery showers could cap the peak near the lower end of the 33–34 °C range. Trader consensus at 65 % for 33 °C and 17–19 % for 32 °C or 34 °C reflects this narrow, well-supported window ahead of the next model update.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models and official guidance point to a peak temperature in Wuhan on August 24, 2026, most likely in the 35–36°C range, aligning with the market’s heaviest positioning at 36°C (44%) and 35°C (25.5%).** 

Wuhan’s subtropical monsoon climate in late August typically features high solar insolation, elevated dew points (often 25–28°C), and urban heat island amplification that can push afternoon readings several degrees above rural surroundings. Current conditions show a lingering heat pattern under partly cloudy skies with scattered showers or thunderstorms possible, which models indicate will introduce enough cloud cover and evaporative cooling to moderate the daily maximum. 

Official Chinese meteorological warnings issued August 23 highlight persistent highs near or above 35°C, with localized potential for 37°C if convection remains limited. Ensemble forecasts (including ECMWF and GFS runs referenced in available guidance) cluster tightly around 34–36°C for the 24th, reflecting steering flow from the east-northeast and modest moisture that favors isolated rather than widespread storms. 

This leaves only a modest 20.5% implied probability on 37°C or higher, consistent with the low odds of completely suppressed convection or stronger subsidence. Historical August climatology shows typical highs near 30–32°C, so the current setup represents above-average heat driven by recent ridge influence, tempered by the day’s expected shower activity. Updated model runs and any revised National Meteorological Center guidance on the morning of the 24th represent the key near-term catalysts that could shift these market-implied odds.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecasts from multiple sources, including Argentina’s Servicio Meteorológico Nacional and international models, point to a daytime maximum near 12–13 °C on August 24 under partly cloudy skies with light easterly winds.** This consensus underpins the market’s heavy weighting toward 13 °C (54 % implied probability), followed by 12 °C and 14 °C.

August is climatologically the coolest month in Buenos Aires, with historical average highs around 15–16 °C, but recent days have run 2–4 °C below normal amid a stable high-pressure pattern. Overnight lows near 6–8 °C and modest daytime heating under limited insolation keep the peak temperature tightly constrained. No significant warm advection or frontal passage is indicated in the latest model runs, reducing the chance of a spike above 14 °C or a drop below 11 °C.

Traders appear to be pricing in this narrow forecast envelope, with very low probabilities assigned to extremes. Updated model guidance and any last-minute observational shifts from the National Meteorological Service will be the key near-term drivers of further adjustments.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zspd

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rpll

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent southwest monsoon flow, or Habagat, is the main factor keeping Manila’s August 25 maximum temperature tightly clustered near 30–32 °C.** Official PAGASA outlooks and short-range global models (GFS, ECMWF) indicate partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers and thunderstorms through the period, which limits daytime heating while moderate southwesterly winds promote mixing. This setup produces market-implied odds favoring 31 °C or 32 °C because even modest differences in convective timing or cloud cover can shift the daily peak by 1 °C. Historical August climatology for Manila centers on 31 °C highs, and current guidance shows no strong deviation from that baseline. Traders are therefore watching the next PAGASA regional forecast and afternoon model runs for any signals of reduced cloudiness or earlier thunderstorm development that could push readings toward the upper or lower edge of the favored range.
